root_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For each fixed integer n greater than 1, define f_n(x) = floor of (n times x) minus the sum for k from 1 to n of (floor of (k times x) divided by k). Determine the set of real x that maximize f_n(x) over all real numbers x, and determine the maximum value of f_n(x).

There exists a real x such that the expression at x is at least the expression at every real y
For all real y, compare the expression value at x versus y

payload.theorem_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

assembly_plan.proof_skeleton_nl: First use integer periodicity to reduce to x in [0,1). The final interval [(n-1)/n,1) is evaluated directly and gives the value H_n-1. On every earlier interval [m/n,(m+1)/n), monotonicity reduces the problem to the left endpoint m/n, and the bottleneck endpoint estimate shows these values are strictly smaller than H_n-1. Therefore the maximizing points in [0,1) are exactly the last interval, and periodicity lifts this to all real x as the fractional-part condition {x} in [(n-1)/n,1). The maximum value is H_n-1.

steps.derives: For an arbitrary real x, write x = z + t with z an integer and t in [0,1). By integer periodicity, F_n(x) = F_n(t), so it is enough to maximize over t in [0,1).
steps.trivial_justification: This uses the standard decomposition of a real number into integer part and fractional part together with periodicity.

steps.derives: For every t in [(n-1)/n,1), F_n(t) = H_n - 1. Hence every point in the last interval already attains the candidate maximum value.
steps.trivial_justification: This is a direct application of the explicit evaluation lemma.

steps.derives: If t lies in an earlier interval [m/n,(m+1)/n) with m <= n-2, then F_n(t) <= F_n(m/n) < H_n - 1. So no point in any earlier interval can maximize.
steps.trivial_justification: The conclusion comes from monotonicity on the interval and then the strict endpoint bound, i.e. two logical steps.

steps.derives: On [0,1), the maximum value of F_n is H_n - 1, and the maximizing points are exactly those t in [(n-1)/n,1).
steps.trivial_justification: Combine the existence of maximizers on the last interval with the exclusion of all earlier intervals.

steps.derives: For all real x, F_n(x) is maximal exactly when its fractional part {x} lies in [(n-1)/n,1). Equivalently, the maximizers are the union over all integers m of [m + (n-1)/n, m + 1), and the maximum value is H_n - 1.
steps.trivial_justification: Translate the [0,1) characterization by integer periodicity and rewrite it in terms of the fractional part.

lemmas.strictly_easier_reason: It is an exact arithmetic reformulation at special rational points, far narrower than the full maximization problem.

candidates.strategy_summary: Reduce by integer periodicity to the fractional part x in [0,1). Then split [0,1) into the intervals [m/n,(m+1)/n). The last interval is easy and gives the candidate value H_n-1 directly. On the earlier intervals, monotonicity reduces everything to the grid points m/n, and a residue-counting plus harmonic-sum estimate shows those grid values are strictly smaller than H_n-1. This identifies both the maximizing set and the maximum value.
